exposure: Current practice related to thromboprophylaxis following cesarean section
outcome: Prevalence of VTE risk assessment using structured checklists/interviews
Proportion of hospitals using universal heparin thromboprophylaxis post C-section
Preferred heparin doses (usual, body weight adjusted, therapeutic)
Duration of heparin thromboprophylaxis for low and increased VTE risk women
Adherence to German and international guidelines for thromboprophylaxis
cohort: Heads of registered departments of obstetrics and gynecology in Germany who responded to a national questionnaire.
finding: The vast majority of hospitals (93%) used heparin prophylaxis after any C-section, irrespective of individual risk factors or the mode of C-section, which is in remarkable contrast to guideline recommendations, and there was wide variation among respondents in heparin dosing and duration related to the VTE risk profile.
mod_finding: The majority of responding hospitals preferred universal heparin thromboprophylaxis following both elective and emergency caesarean section.
cross-section timing: At the time the survey was conducted (approximately 2019-2020).
